notes: Marina is Pebble Beach Systems' playout/distribution AUTOMATION SOFTWARE, not a fixed-I/O hardware device. The official datasheet is explicit that it runs on "standard IT hardware platforms" and is delivered "without reliance on bespoke hardware" — its own tier (core servers, mirrored SQL database, client workstations) communicates purely over generic IP/Ethernet. The datasheet's architecture diagram shows SDI/IP media ports, but those belong to the separate third-party devices Marina controls (VTRs, video servers, "Integrated Channel" units, MCS/GFX/CC-subtitle/UPDOWN boxes) — not to Marina itself. No manufacturer-published physical connector/port list exists for a "Marina" product because it has no fixed hardware SKU: a deployment is sized as a cluster of generic rack servers (e.g. "a typical 16 channel fully redundant system... in 5 servers occupying just 9RU, consuming 3500W" per the datasheet), with network port count depending on the NIC teaming/redundancy configuration chosen by the integrator. The two ports listed here (redundant GbE network, IEC power) are inferred generically from "standard IT hardware" / rack-server implication in the source, not read off any spec table, hence confidence is low. Could not confirm rack unit size for a single node, network port grade/speed, or any true AV signal connectors (there are none — Marina is a control/automation layer, not an AV source/sink device). No dedicated hardware-appliance spec sheet for "Marina" was found on pebble.tv or via reputable AV/broadcast retailers (B&H/Sweetwater/Markertek/Crutchfield do not carry broadcast automation software; a BroadcastStore.com "turnkey system" listing exists but was inaccessible and would in any case reflect an integrator's server choice, not a Pebble Beach spec).
